title: DRAFT: When experts disagree about CVS
review_status: DRAFT pending review by a domain expert
learning_objectives: Interpret a CVS value as the mean of three annotators.
Recognise disagreement (values of 1/3 or 2/3) and suggest reasons for it.
Explain why disagreement matters when reference labels are used to evaluate models.
rubric: DRAFT rubric pending review by a domain expert. Reward careful reasoning about uncertainty in the reference labels.

rubric_criteria.title: Interpreting the values
rubric_criteria.description: Correctly reads a mean of three annotators and identifies disagreement.

rubric_criteria.title: Reasons for disagreement
rubric_criteria.description: Offers plausible, frame-based reasons why annotators might differ.

rubric_criteria.title: Consequences
rubric_criteria.description: Explains how disagreement limits using these labels as ground truth.

blocks.title: Learning objectives
blocks.content: Interpret CVS values as a mean of three annotators, recognise disagreement, and explain why it matters for evaluating models.

blocks.title: How the reference values work
blocks.content: Each CVS value in Endoscapes is the mean of three annotators: 0 means none marked the criterion achieved, 1 means all did, and 1/3 or 2/3 means they disagreed.

blocks.title: Open the frame
blocks.content: This frame was chosen because the annotators disagreed on at least one criterion.

blocks.title: Make your own judgement first
blocks.content: Judge each criterion before you see the annotator values.

blocks.title: Why might experts disagree?
blocks.content: After the reveal, suggest two reasons visible in this frame why annotators might have disagreed.

blocks.title: Labels and models
blocks.content: If a model is scored against these labels, what does annotator disagreement mean for how you read its accuracy?
